name: dev
notes: The dev split of the frozen 72-question benchmark (evaluation.md §1). Split seed 42, stratified by category. The dev split is the tuning split: a weight tuned on it may not be reported on it. The answerable: false rows are built so that EVERY token of the question is absent from the corpus - not only the content tokens - and the generator MEASURES that against a real ingest before it writes the split. The reason is a measured one: the abstention gate is lexical, and the lex component is min-max normalized per query, so a single matching token gives lex = 1.0. Measured on the Civil Code, 'Elucidate zeppelin airship quantum observatory' refuses with no citations, while 'How does a zeppelin airship quantum observatory work?' is ANSWERED with 8 citations - the difference is entirely the scaffolding words, which occur in the corpus. A planted unanswerable question that shares ordinary vocabulary with the corpus is therefore ANSWERED, with citations, and the abstention metric then measures the dataset rather than the system. The honest limitation: refusing a question whose vocabulary is absent is a WEAKER test than refusing a question that is out-of-domain in substance. The abstention score this split produces is a lower bound on the system's refusal quality, not a measurement of it.

questions.question: Compare how a legal separation is granted and how it takes effect on the spouses' property.
expected_claims: no decree upon a stipulation of facts
questions.notes: 101 is the grant and 104 the effect.

questions.question: Compare the ownership of a swarm of bees with the ownership of pigeons and fish that fly to another owner.
expected_claims: the owner of a swarm of bees
provided they have not been enticed
questions.notes: Two adjacent acquisition articles with different conditions.

questions.question: How do the effects of legal separation on the spouses differ from its effects on the family home?
expected_claims: the family home shall be dissolved
cease to be exempt from execution
questions.notes: The same pair as the multi-section row above, asked as a comparison. The questions differ; the golds are the same provisions.

questions.question: Article 120 refers to the persons designated by law to give consent to the marriage of a minor. What does article 121 require for a modification of the marriage settlements?
expected_claims: made before the celebration of the marriage
subject to the provisions of Art. 191
questions.notes: The question names the consent article to lead to the modification article.

questions.question: Article 1624 refers to article 1475. What does article 1475 provide about the perfection of the contract of sale?
expected_claims: perfected at the moment there is a meeting of minds
upon the thing which is the object
questions.notes: The cited provision is the rule on when a sale is perfected. Article 1466 is the construing distractor.

questions.question: Article 718 grants the finder of hidden treasure the right given by article 438. What does article 438 provide?
questions.notes: A direct cross-reference. The treasure article is short, and 719 is the found-movable distractor.

questions.question: What does the Code call the part of the testator's property that cannot be disposed of in favour of the compulsory heirs?
questions.notes: A paraphrase question: the question never says 'legitime', so this row tests whether the answer can be located without the term.

questions.question: What is a substitution in the law of succession?
expected_claims: in default of the heir originally instituted
questions.notes: The definition article for substitution. Articles 860-868 are its distractors.

questions.question: What is the rule for a movable that is not treasure and is found by someone else?
expected_claims: must return it to its previous possessor
questions.notes: A rule expressed as a procedure. The gold is the found-movable article, not the treasure article beside it.

questions.question: What does Article 1231 provide about the causes that extinguish obligations?
questions.notes: Carried over from the golden 10Q, reworded to name the article. The gold is the enumerated list, not one of the items.

questions.question: What does Article 3 provide about ignorance of the law?
questions.notes: Carried over from the golden 10Q. A short provision (under the 50-character evidence floor) and the identified node's exemption from it is what makes this row interesting.

questions.question: What does Article 361 provide about juvenile courts?
questions.notes: Carried over from the golden 10Q. The shortest gold in the dataset, which makes it a good test of the evidence floor.

questions.question: What does Article 774 define as succession?
expected_claims: by his will or by operation of law
questions.notes: Carried over from the golden 10Q.

questions.question: What must the vendor return when he exercises the right of repurchase?
questions.notes: The central provision of the redemption chapter. Articles 1617 and 1618 are its neighbours.

questions.question: Article 2000 makes the hotel-keeper responsible for the loss of guests' property. What does article 2001 say about the act of a thief?
questions.notes: A second route to the same gold as the row above, worded differently. The gold is the same provision; the questions are not.

questions.question: Recite quantum spectrometer embargo
questions.notes: Unanswerable: 'recite', 'quantum', 'spectrometer' and 'embargo' are absent from the corpus. The verb is part of the constraint: 'define' occurs in the U.S. Code Title 11 corpus, and a question whose verb is a word the corpus contains can be answered by vocabulary alone.

questions.question: Under what exception is a minor who may not contract marriage without parental consent still able to acknowledge a natural child?
questions.notes: Article 279's own exception. Article 281 is the child-of-age distractor.

questions.question: A contract is voidable under article 1390. Which article provides for the requisites of a contract, and what are they?
questions.notes: The question reaches the voidability list and then the requisites, so the answer needs both articles.

questions.question: How is the obligation extinguished by a payment made by one of the solidary debtors, and what may that debtor claim from his co-debtors?
expected_claims: Payment made by one of the solidary debtors extinguishes the obligation
the creditor may choose which offer to accept
claim from his co-debtors only the share that corresponds to each
questions.notes: 1217 is the payment and 1216 the creditor's right to proceed against any one of the solidary debtors. Article 1214 is the payment-to-one-creditor distractor.

questions.question: What is a legacy or devise of a thing that belongs to another person, and when is it void?
expected_claims: limited to such part or interest
erroneously believed that the thing pertained to him
questions.notes: 929 limits the legacy and 930 makes it void on the testator's mistake. Article 931 is the acquisition distractor.

questions.question: How is the partition of a thing owned in common made, and what accounting follows it?
expected_claims: by agreement between the parties or by judicial proceedings
damages caused by reason of his negligence or fraud
questions.notes: 496 is the manner and 500 the accounting. Article 494 (the right to demand partition) is the distractor.

questions.question: What are the effects of legal separation on the spouses, and on the family home?
expected_claims: the family home shall be dissolved
cease to be exempt from execution
questions.notes: 104 is the effect on the spouses and 237 the effect on the family home.

questions.question: What are the requisites for the celebration of marriage, and who may solemnize it?
questions.notes: Article 53 lists the requisites and 56 lists who may solemnize. Article 57 is the place-of-solemnization distractor.

questions.question: What happens to parental authority, and when does it terminate?
questions.notes: 313 states the rule and 327 the four terminating events. Article 321 is the usufruct-over-the-child's-property distractor.
